exchange_rates.spread_note: Parallel premium over official = 8.52/6.3732 ≈ 33.7%. For COD revenue analysis, LYD collected in cash converts to USD at the PARALLEL rate (~8.5), not the official rate, unless the importer has CBL letter-of-credit access at the official rate.

china_to_libya_sea_lcl.per_kg_equivalence_estimate: ESTIMATE: at ~150 USD/CBM and a typical 200 kg/CBM parcel density, sea LCL ≈ $0.75/kg + fixed clearance costs — roughly 10x cheaper than air but 3-6x slower. Reasoning-based conversion, not a quoted per-kg rate.

shipping.100_unit_relevance_note: ESTIMATE: a ~100-unit consignment of the light products here (shapewear/jewelry/gloves: <0.5 kg/unit, <0.5 CBM total) is below LCL minimums (2 CBM at Misrata consolidators), so realistic options are air standard at $5.5-12/kg or piggy-backing on a consolidator's groupage at the ~$150/CBM+min charge. Heavier items (door lock ~1kg+, ice-cream kit) shift the math toward sea groupage.
shipping.battery_caveat: P06 (toothbrush) and P12 (shaver) contain lithium batteries; P03 likely does. Battery goods are restricted/ surcharged on air freight — sea or special battery-line air is typically required (estimate/reasoning, no single source; consistent with standard freight practice).

customs.structure: Libya abolished traditional customs duties on most goods in Aug 2005; imports instead pay a 4% Port Services Tax on CIF value, plus category-specific Production Tax (2%) and Consumption Tax (25% or 50%) on regulated products. No VAT.

import_tax_2026.context: New import tax law moved to implementation by CBL as the dollar passed 10 LYD (early 2026); Tripoli government contested it. Rates should be confirmed at HS-code level.

customs.compliance: Importers need a CBL Letter of Credit, Electronic Cargo Tracking Note (ECTN), Arabic labeling, pre-shipment Certificate of Inspection, and Ministry of Economy product registration. Source: https://carraglobe.com/importer-of-record-libya/ (via search snippet)

shipeh.what: Shipeh (https://shipeh.com/) is a COD e-commerce fulfillment platform 'empowering entrepreneurs to launch, grow and scale e-commerce ventures across Iraq and Libya' — shipping, warehousing, customs clearance, COD collection and seller remittance; recently launched a 'COD Drop' feature (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DO83RHQiHs5/). Site returns 403 to direct fetch; no published Libya fee schedule found.
shipeh.simulation_benchmarks: Shipeh's own 'Simulation' planning documents (Scribd) use these baseline metrics — Iraq version: confirmation rate 50%, delivery rate 50%, return fee $150 (interpretation of return fee unclear from snippet; possibly per-simulation batch). A parallel 'Shipeh Simulation (Libya) V2.0' document exists but its figures were not extractable from search snippets.

libya_specific.implied_delivery_economics: If Shipeh's planning assumptions (50% confirmation of placed orders, 50% delivery of confirmed) are representative, only ~25% of raw COD orders convert to collected cash — a critical margin input. Labeled: sourced from Shipeh's own simulation docs, but they are planning templates, not audited performance data.
libya_specific.market_context: Libya e-commerce is small: most Libyan online stores do <$100/month in sales (https://www.aftership.com/ecommerce/statistics/regions/ly); e-commerce 'does not play a significant role' per https://www.lloydsbanktrade.com/en/market-potential/libya/ecommerce. Facebook/Instagram shops with COD to 'all Libyan cities' are the dominant retail channel (e.g. https://www.facebook.com/OlympiaStoreLYD/videos/945928416967511/ — dental kit at 75 LYD + nationwide COD delivery).

cod_return_rates.note: No audited Libya-specific COD return-rate figure exists publicly. Best available anchors: Shipeh's own 50%/50% planning rates (above), UAE 20% COD return rate, and the generic 15-30% COD-vs-prepaid refusal delta. A Libya COD refusal rate of 25-40% remains a reasonable ESTIMATE (cash-only market, weak addressing, higher friction than UAE).

notes: All Libyan domains (cbl.gov.ly, libyaobserver.ly, libyaakhbar.com, ly.opensooq.com, ubuy.com.ly, meam.ly, dollar2day.com) returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch from this environment; every LYD figure therefore comes from WebSearch result snippets and is dated where the snippet allowed. Key takeaway: the official/parallel FX spread (~6.37 vs ~8.52, ~34%) is the single biggest margin variable for a COD importer. meam.ly is a confirmed live Libyan online store useful for retail price benchmarking (SHEIN-sourced goods: shapewear 51 LYD, gold-plated necklace set 21 LYD).
